rules.message: force push rewrites shared history; push a new commit or ask the operator
--no-verify skips the hooks; fix the finding instead
git commit -n skips the hooks; fix the finding instead
push to a protected branch; push a feature branch and open a pull request
gh api with a mutating method; use a read-only call (fields only with an explicit -X GET), ops/conductor/gh_ops.py or ask the operator
pushing every ref can overwrite or delete protected branches; push one feature branch
--admin bypasses branch protection; wait for the required checks and reviews
changing core.hooksPath switches the git hooks off; ask the operator
git -c core.hooksPath switches the git hooks off; ask the operator
a command piped or fed into a shell is hidden from the guard; run the command directly
re-baselining, anchoring and syncing the controls is the operator's step; deliver a patch and ask
moving or removing the reference the gates compare against is the operator's step; ask
hiding changes from git hides them from the gates; ask the operator
piping a download into a shell runs unreviewed code; download, read, then run
GATES_OFFLINE turns missing tools into skips; run the gates as they are
a token with a known vendor prefix ends up in logs; read it from the environment
a secret literal in a command ends up in logs; read it from the environment
bypassing the permission checks switches every deny rule off; run claude with the project settings
a release runs only through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py dispatch-release; never dispatch or create it directly (name a workflow by file, not by id)
pushing a tag starts a release; the release goes through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py dispatch-release only
push.followTags pushes tags with every push; the release goes through ops/conductor/gh_ops.py dispatch-release only
fetching into a remote-tracking ref moves the reference the gates compare against; plain git fetch only
git -c remote.* rewires where fetch writes or reads; plain git fetch only

write_rules.message: a secret literal must not be written into a file; read it from the environment or a secret store
a token with a known vendor prefix must not be written into a file
a private key must not be written into a file
